name: Amritsar
shortDescription: Amritsar is both a sacred city and an energetic food town, with the Golden Temple at its heart and difficult history never far away.
description:
Most visits naturally begin at the Golden Temple, but do not treat it as a box to tick. Go once in daylight and, if time allows, return after dark when the marble complex takes on a quieter glow. The community kitchen is part of the experience, whether you eat there or volunteer for a simple task.

Jallianwala Bagh sits close by and asks for a very different mood. Give it proper attention before entering the surrounding market streets. The Partition Museum adds the wider human story and is worth more than a hurried half-hour.

Amritsar is compact around the historic centre. Stay within walking distance if these places are your priority, and treat the Wagah–Attari ceremony as a separate excursion with security and traffic time built in.
bestTimeToVisit: October to March brings the easiest walking weather, although winter mornings can be foggy and cold. April to June is intensely hot. Monsoon humidity and showers arrive from July into September.
budgetEstimate: ₹1,700–5,500 per person per day (excluding intercity travel)

topAttractions.name: Golden Temple
topAttractions.description: The Harmandir Sahib complex welcomes visitors of all backgrounds. Cover your head, wash your feet, leave shoes at the designated counter and move with the flow of worshippers.
topAttractions.timings: Open daily; busiest around ceremonies and holidays

topAttractions.name: Jallianwala Bagh
topAttractions.description: A memorial to the 1919 massacre. Read the interpretation and allow space for reflection rather than treating the preserved marks as photo props.

topAttractions.name: Partition Museum
topAttractions.description: Personal accounts and objects tell the story of Partition with unusual emotional clarity. It can be heavy, so avoid squeezing it between rushed stops.

topAttractions.name: Gobindgarh Fort
topAttractions.description: A restored fort with exhibits and programmed performances; useful for families, though the presentation is more theatrical than the historic centre.

topAttractions.name: Durgiana Temple
topAttractions.description: A Hindu temple complex built around a sacred pool, close to the railway side of central Amritsar.

topAttractions.name: Ram Bagh Palace and Garden
topAttractions.description: The summer-palace grounds connect the city with Maharaja Ranjit Singh; check which museum areas are currently open.

topAttractions.name: Attari–Wagah border ceremony
topAttractions.description: A highly choreographed daily military ceremony west of the city. Carry minimal belongings and allow generous time for security and traffic.

topAttractions.name: Hall Bazaar
topAttractions.description: A busy market for textiles, juttis, spices and everyday shopping, reached through the Gandhi Gate.

localFood.name: Amritsari Kulcha
localFood.description: Tandoor-baked stuffed bread served with chole, onion and chutney; breakfast or lunch is the natural time for it.

localFood.name: Langar
localFood.description: A simple vegetarian meal prepared and served collectively at the Golden Temple. Sit with everyone and follow volunteer guidance.

localFood.name: Amritsari Fish
localFood.description: River fish in a spiced gram-flour coating, fried crisp and served with chutney.
localFood.whereToTry: Established fish shops outside the sacred precinct

localFood.name: Chole Bhature
localFood.description: A filling plate of chickpeas and fried bread that works best as a late breakfast.

localFood.name: Lassi
localFood.description: Thick, cool and often topped with malai; one glass can be closer to a snack than a drink.

localFood.name: Phirni
localFood.description: Slow-set ground-rice pudding served chilled in small clay bowls.

tips: Cover your head and dress modestly.
Keep shoes at the official counter.
Photography is restricted in important areas; follow signs.
Use an e-rickshaw or auto for nearby stops.
Book Wagah transport with a clear return plan.
Carry a warm layer for winter mornings.
Expect summer afternoons to be punishing.
Fog can affect winter trains and flights.
Share rich dishes so you can try more than one.
Eat kulcha while it is fresh from the tandoor.
Keep the sacred precinct free of tobacco and alcohol.

hiddenGems: Pul Kanjari - A small historic stop near the border route, best visited with planned transport.
Khairuddin Mosque - A central mosque connected with the freedom movement.
Ram Tirath - A religious complex outside the city associated with the Ramayana tradition.
Company Bagh mornings - The Ram Bagh grounds feel most local before the day becomes busy.
Qila Ahluwalia lanes - Old-city streets where architecture survives above the shopfronts.
Gurudwara Baba Atal Rai - A distinctive tower close to the Golden Temple with its own devotional importance.

faq.question: How long should I stay in Amritsar?
faq.answer: Two days is comfortable: one for the sacred and historic centre, and another for museums, food and the border excursion.

faq.question: Can non-Sikhs visit the Golden Temple?
faq.answer: Yes. Visitors of all faiths are welcome when they follow the complex’s dress and conduct rules.

faq.question: Is the Wagah ceremony essential?
faq.answer: No. It is popular and theatrical, but travellers more interested in history may prefer extra time at the Partition Museum.

faq.question: Where is the easiest place to stay?
faq.answer: Near the Golden Temple if you want early and late visits; around Ranjit Avenue for a quieter, more modern base.
